questions.q: The Court puts the unofficial divide between the Rhône's two halves at Montélimar. Which city does it call the main city of the south?
questions.exp: Avignon, the papal city of the fourteenth century, anchors the southern Rhône, with Châteauneuf-du-Pape just to its north; Lyon lies above the northern end of the valley, and the vines thin out for some fifty kilometres between Valence and Montélimar. The Court asks a Certified candidate to place all three cities.

questions.q: A red Côtes du Rhône Villages must hold at least what share of Grenache?
questions.exp: Côtes du Rhône Villages red must be at least half Grenache, with Syrah and Mourvèdre together at least a fifth, while plain Côtes du Rhône red from the southern zone needs at least 30 per cent Grenache. The Court's Certified wine law row asks these Grenache minimums beside the 12.5 per cent alcohol floor of Châteauneuf-du-Pape.

questions.q: Grenache brings warmth and sweet red fruit to a southern blend. Which weakness of the grape do Syrah and Mourvèdre make good?
opts: Pale colour and a tendency to oxidise
Low alcohol and a thin body
questions.exp: Grenache ripens to high sugar and alcohol with generous fruit but carries little colour and soft tannin, and its wine browns and oxidises early. Syrah adds colour, structure and dark fruit, and Mourvèdre adds tannin and a resistance to oxidation, which is why the Court asks why the south blends rather than bottling single varieties as the north does.

questions.q: A guest who loves rich, barrel-fermented Chardonnay wants to try something from the Rhône instead. Which wine would you pour?
questions.exp: White Hermitage, mostly Marsanne with Roussanne, is full, broad and waxy with modest acidity and ages for decades, so it fills the place of a rich Chardonnay at table; Condrieu's Viognier does the same with more perfume. Tavel is a dry rosé, Cornas a tannic Syrah and Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise a sweet fortified wine.

questions.q: Which description fits Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise as the Court sets out its style?
opts: Fully fortified and aged in solera
Unfortified and aged in new oak
Lightly fortified and aged oxidatively in glass
questions.exp: Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise is a vin doux naturel: neutral grape spirit stops the fermentation of Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, leaving sweetness at about 15 per cent alcohol, and the wine is bottled young without oak to keep its grape and orange blossom aroma. Serve it cold with fruit desserts.

questions.q: Many modern southern Rhône vineyards are trained on wires rather than as gobelet bush vines. What chiefly drives that change?
questions.exp: A trellis lets a tractor and a harvesting machine work the row, so the Court notes that modern southern plantings are often trellised for economic reasons. The traditional gobelet does the other three jobs: it shades its own bunches, stands low against the mistral and needs little water, which is why old Grenache is still grown that way.

questions.q: Name one of the geographical names a grower may add after Côtes du Rhône Villages on a label.
questions.ans: Séguret (also Sablet, Visan, Valréas, Plan de Dieu and others)
questions.exp: Above plain Côtes du Rhône Villages stand the Villages with a geographical name, among them Séguret, Sablet, Visan, Valréas, Roaix, Rochegude and the multi-commune area of Plan de Dieu, each with lower yields and stricter rules. Villages that prove themselves are promoted to cru, as Cairanne was in 2015 and Laudun in 2024, and then leave the Côtes du Rhône name off the label.
